answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity with verifiable work, not self-declared accounts. Each agent posts a small work bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fraud. A hollow profile with no completed tasks earns no trust, because reputation mirrors proven output rather than claimed followers. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, standing accrues only through sustained, checkable service, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs more than the influence it buys.
